claims.text: Advanced classical molecular dynamics can be used to study the thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The molecular dynamics method should incorporate accelerated sampling such as replica-exchange molecular dynamics.
A specifically tailored many-body interatomic potential for FeCuCrCoNi should be used.
The thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles is highly size-dependent.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles exhibit surface melting earlier than larger particles.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles undergo atomic rearrangements earlier than larger particles.
The initial materials are as-synthesized FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Heating and cooling simulations should span ambient temperature to temperatures approaching melting.
The simulations should compare particles ranging from below 10 nm to larger sizes.
Thermal treatment produces atomic-scale lattice distortions in the nanoparticles.
Thermal treatment can produce surface segregation in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Thermal treatment is associated with enhanced atomic diffusion in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The higher surface-to-volume ratio of smaller nanoparticles causes enhanced thermal agitation.
Enhanced thermal agitation in smaller nanoparticles activates atomic diffusion at lower temperatures.
Earlier atomic diffusion in smaller nanoparticles promotes earlier phase changes.
Accelerated sampling overcomes kinetic barriers and reveals size-dependent thermal effects that may be missed by standard molecular dynamics.
Decreasing nanoparticle size lowers the onset temperature for significant structural reorganization, including surface melting or phase separation.
Quantitative transition temperatures depend on the validity of the interatomic potential and sampling method.
Predicted transition temperatures and diffusion rates are uncertain because of potential accuracy and the limited timescale accessible to molecular dynamics.
The hypothesis is falsified if thermal-transition onset does not vary clearly with particle size or if enhanced and standard molecular dynamics show no relevant difference.
